seed: Camera keys ease in and out like every other key (task camera-keys-ease-in-and-out-like-every-other-key), at Next defaults with no flag changed. On a recording, the frame is picked and Camera depth is keyed 0 at one second and 400 at three: a push in. A right click on each Camera row diamond offers the eases a layer's key offers, ticked Ease In and Out as a fresh key moves; both are set to Linear from there, and the Camera section's Curve row reads Linear. Undo takes the second diamond's change back in one step. A picked diamond eases from the timeline bar's Easing too, and the Curve row sets the stretch back to Ease in out. A click on a diamond is a SwiftUI tap, which answers only in the app in front, so this walk takes the front, as camera-keys-row-walk does.

steps.comment: A right click on a diamond: the eases a layer's key offers, ticked where every camera key there agrees.

steps.note: THE FIRST TEST: right-clicking the first Camera row diamond offers Linear, Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In and Out, Hold and Bezier, as a key on a layer's lane does, with Ease In and Out ticked, then Go to Key, Show Camera Settings and Delete Key

steps.comment: The Camera section: the Curve row speaks for the stretch the playhead is in.

steps.note: THE SECOND TEST: both diamonds set to Linear from their right-click menus; with the frame picked at two seconds, the Camera section's Curve row reads Linear and the diamonds on the Camera row are drawn as linear keys

steps.comment: Undo takes the second diamond's ease back in one step: the stretch is no longer all linear.
A picked diamond eases from the timeline bar's Easing, as picked keys do.

steps.note: THE THIRD TEST: the first diamond picked, the timeline bar shows Easing reading Linear; choosing Ease In and Out there eases the diamond, and with both ends eased the Camera section's Curve row reads Ease in out

steps.comment: The Curve row sets the stretch from the panel, with a shape no pair of keys makes.

steps.note: THE FOURTH TEST: Ease out back chosen on the Camera section's Curve row; the push in overshoots and settles
